items.title: Godfrey Hirsch Interview, 1987-10-20
items.q: I made Henry Newfield a leader at the Court of the Two Sisters... he needed a band. So I asked Henry if he wanted to work on it.

ctx.x: Yeah, I just didn't know you worked with him.

Yeah, he was with, Pat was with me for ages. In fact, I got, I got, I made Henry Newfield a leader at the Court of the Two Sisters. Joe Fine is a very dear friend of mine. I've known Joe all my life almost. And I was his music advisor down at the, at the, at the Court of the Two Sisters. Uh-huh. And, uh, he needed a band. So I asked Henry if he wanted to work on it. And he got, he got that little, the barber, the piano player. And, uh, he had Pat on bass. He was, I don't remember who played trumpet with him. But,…
What did you call him, uh, that plays piano? From across the river? Valentino, Valentino.

items.title: Godfrey Hirsch Interview, 1987-10-27
items.q: I know, Louis Macenta, Henry Newfield, and several guys... they were taking summer courses at Loyola to get credits so that they would have enough so that they would be legitimate to be able to teach in the public school system.

ctx.x: You'd hit a certain note on the Wagner phone... And everything would explode. You know the old glass... Vibrations. The Wagner phone was gonna do it. Without a doubt... He finally, after he gave up music... He became a professor down at one of the high schools down there. The one that was... I think it was Nichols. ! Where they had the Confederate flag. I mean, they had a lot of trouble down there with the Confederate flag. And, uh... Because the colored people didn't like the Confederate flag. So he left the…
